From 46c6d45d7875a0328258a574e376ae75f7b2a64b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2015 23:35:25 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] cxlflash: off by one bug in cxlflash_show_port_status()

The > should be >= or we read one element past the end of the array.

Fixes: c21e0bbfc485 ('cxlflash: Base support for IBM CXL Flash Adapter')
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Acked-by: Matthew R. Ochs <mrochs@linux.vnet.ibm.com>
Signed-off-by: James Bottomley <JBottomley@Odin.com>

diff --git a/drivers/scsi/cxlflash/main.c b/drivers/scsi/cxlflash/main.c
index 458ed838f83a..fde2ba9342dc 100644
--- a/drivers/scsi/cxlflash/main.c
+++ b/drivers/scsi/cxlflash/main.c
@@ -586,7 +586,7 @@ static ssize_t cxlflash_show_port_status(struct device *dev,
 	u64 *fc_regs;
 
 	rc = kstrtouint((attr->attr.name + 4), 10, &port);
-	if (rc || (port > NUM_FC_PORTS))
+	if (rc || (port >= NUM_FC_PORTS))
 		return 0;
 
 	fc_regs = &afu->afu_map->global.fc_regs[port][0];
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/scsi/cxlflash/main.c`**
- The condition in the `cxlflash_show_port_status` function was modified from:
  ```c
  if (rc || (port > NUM_FC_PORTS))
  ```
  to:
  ```c
  if (rc || (port >= NUM_FC_PORTS))
  ```
  This change ensures that the code does not read one element past the end of the array by using `>=` instead of `>`.

### Relationships
The modification addresses an off-by-one bug in the `cxlflash_show_port_status` function, which could lead to accessing an invalid memory location. The change is directly related to the handling of the `port` variable, ensuring that it remains within valid bounds defined by `NUM_FC_PORTS`. This fix is part of a broader effort to improve the stability and correctness of the cxlflash driver, as indicated by the associated fix reference.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (rc || (port > NUM_FC_PORTS))
fc_regs = &afu->afu_map->global.fc_regs[port][0];
```
Reason:
The condition `port > NUM_FC_PORTS` allows the `port` variable to exceed the valid index range of the `fc_regs` array, which can lead to accessing an out-of-bounds memory location. This results in undefined behavior or crashes when trying to read from an invalid memory address.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (rc || (port >= NUM_FC_PORTS))
fc_regs = &afu->afu_map->global.fc_regs[port][0];
```
Reason:
Changing the condition to `port >= NUM_FC_PORTS` ensures that the `port` variable remains within the valid index range of the `fc_regs` array, thus preventing out-of-bounds access and ensuring safe memory operations.
